t: Listen to a talk in an ecology class.
Let's look at an invasive plant called garlic mustard, which arrived in North America from Europe.
Garlic mustard releases chemicals into the soil.
These chemicals harm certain fungi that live on the roots of native trees.
Those fungi help the trees absorb water and nutrients.
So when the fungi decline, young native trees grow more slowly.
Over time, the forest floor has fewer native seedlings and more garlic mustard.
Notice that the plant doesn't attack the trees directly.
Some deer also avoid eating it, but researchers still disagree about how much that matters.
